intro_html: Broccoli cheddar soup energy, rebuilt as a one-pot dinner: creamy cheddar rice, browned turkey, and a crispy parmesan crumb topping. Every serving packs 35 grams of protein for about $1.78, which makes it one of the cheapest bowls in this whole section.
cost_closing_html: About $1.78 a bowl for what a soup-and-bread chain charges $8, and theirs comes with maybe a third of the protein and no second helping in your fridge.
shop_smart: Frozen broccoli florets at three bags for $3.49 beat fresh crowns on price, prep time, and waste. They go straight from freezer to pot.
The cheddar is the second biggest line at $3.02. Buy the 8 oz bags on sale and check the block cheese price; shredding your own usually wins per ounce.
The milk costs 27 cents here because the rest of the gallon goes to breakfast. Whole ingredients you already buy weekly are the cheapest ingredients there are.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat most of the olive oil in your biggest pot. Brown the ground turkey, breaking it up, until it reaches 165F with no pink remaining. Add the onion and cook until soft, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the rinsed rice, chicken broth, oregano, basil, paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cover and simmer about 15 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.
Stir in the milk, Dijon mustard, and broccoli florets. Cover and cook 5 more minutes until the broccoli is bright and tender.
Pull the pot off the heat and stir in the cheddar a handful at a time until the whole thing turns creamy.
In a small skillet, toast the bread crumbs in the butter until golden, then stir in the parmesan.
Portion into 14 containers and sprinkle the crumb topping over each so it stays crisp.
portion_html: Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty pot number you wrote down, and divide by 14. Scoop that weight into each container, add the crumb topping, and every bowl lands at about 592 calories and 35 grams of protein.

steps: Brown the turkey to 165F with onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add rice, broth, and seasonings; cover and simmer until the rice is nearly tender.
Stir in milk, Dijon, and broccoli; cook 5 minutes, then stir in cheddar off the heat.
Toast bread crumbs in butter with parmesan and top each of the 14 portions.
